newsitem.title: USA: FBI casts global net in letter bomb investigation.
newsitem.headline: FBI casts global net in letter bomb investigation.

text.p: The FBI cast a global net on Friday in its investigation of at least seven letter bombs mailed from Egypt to the United States, sending an attache to Alexandria and asking friendly foreign intelligence sources for help.
An eighth suspicious letter that the FBI said appeared to be a bomb was intercepted at a post office in Kansas on Friday.

"We are not only conducting the investigation in the United States, but also are reaching out to friendly foreign intelligence sources to see if they have anything that might be of interest," FBI spokeswoman Susan Lloyd said.

Lloyd said the FBI has asked its legal attache in Egypt to travel to the Egyptian city of Alexandria, which was the postmark on some of the bombs. Seven of the bombs were disguised as Christmas cards and mailed from Egypt, the FBI said earlier.

Lloyd said the investigation of the devices -- four of which were found at the Washington offices of the Saudi-owned newspaper Al-Hayat, one at the Washington central post office, two at the federal prison in Leavenworth, Kansas, and one at a post office in Kansas -- as in its earliest stages.

"At this point, it's still early on in the investigation," she said. "We haven't eliminated any possibilities. As far as enumerating who our suspects might be, it's still too early to do that either."
An eighth device, apparently a bomb addressed to Leavenworth prison, was found on Friday at a post office in Kansas, police said. The device did not explode and was given to the FBI.
FBI spokesman in Kansas City, Missouri, said the letter intercepted on Friday was "very similar if not identical to the two delivered yesterday" and it "appeared to be an explosive device."
Lloyd said the FBI was reviewing debris from four devices found on Thursday at Al-Hayat's offices. The devices were "disrupted" safely by the Washington bomb squad.
The first two devices discovered at the Leavenworth prison were being shipped to the FBI's laboratory in Washington, Lloyd said.
The letter bombs were meant to explode when opened, but all were intercepted before they went off, the FBI said, adding that the devices would have caused "grave harm" if detonated.
The FBI said on Thursday there might be more such bombs in the mail and urged Americans to be alert for the devices.

The four devices discovered at the Al-Hayat offices in the National Press building forced the evacuation of dozens of U.S. and foreign news personnel. The press building is located two blocks from the White House.

Lloyd dismissed as "purely speculative" reports that the officials were investigating a possible connection between the cards and key figures in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Centre and the foiled plot to bomb other New York landmarks.
